name: switch
title: Switch
description: A control that toggles between on and off, with a thumb that travels between the two states.
docs:
## When to use - A setting that takes effect immediately: public/private, alerts on/off, a feature flag. - A row in a settings list, where the label describes the thing and the switch describes its state. - A preference with no submit button. Flipping it saves. ## When not to use - The change is only applied on submit; use `checkbox`, which is the familiar form control for a pending decision. - One of several options; use `radio-group`. - A formatting command on a selection; use `toggle`. ## Installation ```bash npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/switch ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { Switch } from "@/components/cadence/switch/switch"; import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label/label"; export function Public() { return (
); } ``` ## Examples ### Sizes ```tsx ``` `size="sm"` keeps the same travel logic: the distance is measured from the track and the thumb, so restyling either keeps the end position correct. ### Controlled ```tsx const [on, setOn] = useState(false); ; ``` ### In a settings row ```tsx

``` ### Disabled ```tsx ``` Disabled switches stay visible and announced; hiding them loses the information that the setting exists. ## API | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ----------------- | --------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------- | | `checked` | `boolean` | – | Controlled state. | | `defaultChecked` | `boolean` | `false` | Uncontrolled initial state. | | `onCheckedChange` | `(checked, details) => void`| – | Fired on click and on Space. | | `size` | `"sm" \| "default"` | `"default"` | Track and thumb scale. | | `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Ignores interaction and form submission. | | `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Focusable, submitted, not changeable. | | `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Blocks submit until switched on. | | `name`, `value` | `string` | – | Form field identity and submitted value. | | `className` | `string` | – | Merged last. | ## Motion contract Recipe: `state.morph`. The thumb travels from one end of the track to the other while the track recolours. The travel distance is measured from the rendered track and thumb — no hard-coded pixel value — so a custom size still lands flush. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------- | | on | `translateX 0 → track − thumb` | `state.morph` | yes | | off | the same distance, reversed | `state.morph` | yes | | reduced | no travel animation; the thumb jumps to the new end | – | – | | none | no transition | – | – | Under `reduced` the thumb still ends up in the right place: position is state, not decoration. What is dropped is the animation, so the movement is instant. ## Keyboard interactions | Keys | Action | | ------- | --------------------------------------- | | `Tab` | Moves focus to the switch. | | `Space` | Toggles the switch, unless `readOnly`. | | `Enter` | Does not toggle — that is native button behaviour, and a switch is not a button. | ## Accessibility - Base UI renders `role="switch"` with `aria-checked` and a hidden input, so the value is submitted with the form. - The state is not carried by colour alone: the thumb position, the track colour, and `aria-checked` change together. - Give it a name with `Label htmlFor` or `aria-label`. "On" is a state, not a name. - A switch that saves immediately should announce the outcome (a `toast` or an inline status), because there is no submit step to confirm it. ## Validation and data ownership | The component does | You do | | ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- | | Forwards `name`, `value`, `disabled`, `required` | Persisting the setting and handling failures | | Exposes `aria-invalid` styling | Deciding whether the switch needs one at all | | Renders the on/off state | Announcing that the change was saved | There is no `validate` or `schema` prop. See [validation](/docs/validation). ## Responsive behavior The control is fixed-size at every breakpoint; the row around it is what changes. In a narrow layout, let the label and description wrap above the switch instead of shrinking the track. ## Performance One `ResizeObserver` per switch measures the travel, so a font or layout change does not desynchronise the thumb. The animation itself is a single `transform` transition with no layout reads during interaction. ## Notes for AI - Use `switch` only for immediate settings. If there is a Save button, use `checkbox`. - Do not animate the track colour as motion; colour is state feedback. - Keep the label outside the switch. A switch with no label has no accessible name.
